blockNote: Option windows of the choice menus: Yes / No, Yes, Record / Move / Quit, Record / Quit and Stay / Go back (file offsets 85762-85875, SNES $02:CF02-$CF73, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

A string here is only the option window, never the question: the question is the COP [01] dialogue printed just before. Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts: 18 Yes / No, 6 Stay / Go back, 1 each of the other three) prints the string with PrintTextString, then calls RunChoiceMenu with the option count from its own operand, and stores the chosen index in choice_result ($03D0). Cop02_PromptYesNo (no script uses it) always prints ChoiceYesNoText.

Layout rule shared by all five strings: [CUR:o] is the window origin (BG3 byte offset, row = o / $40, column = (o mod $40) / 2; every window starts in column 4 and ends on tile row 15: origin row + h + 1 = 15), [07:w,h] draws the frame (w equals the widest option line including its leading blank, h is two tile rows per option), and every option is one text line with a leading blank (the arrow cell). Options are separated by [N][N] because a text line is two tiles tall. The trailing [CUR:c] draws nothing: c = origin + $82 (one row-pair down, one column right) is the cursor cell of the first option, and PrintTextString returns it in X, which is exactly what RunChoiceMenu expects.
The option count in the COP operand must equal the number of lines in the string: the string does not carry it.
=== NOTES ===
- Which actor asks which string is documented at each part; the questions themselves are in the actor files.

- 'Record' is the walkthrough's saving at the Master's Shrine ('go there to heal and save if wanted', 06-dr-leos-lab.md). The 'Move' entry of ChoiceRecordMoveQuitText is not described by the walkthrough (OQ-I030-1).

blockNote: Choice menu: the arrow cursor list of every question window (file offsets 74369-74506, SNES $02:A281-$A30A, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

RunChoiceMenu is called by Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts) and Cop02_PromptYesNo (no script uses it) after the option window of shared_choice_prompt_texts has been printed. A = number of options (8 bit), the high byte of A (read with XBA) = the start index (both callers pass 0), X = BG3 byte offset of the first option's arrow cell. Options are $80 bytes apart (two tile rows). The selected index is kept on the stack ($01,S) for the whole menu; menu_count ($03C4) holds the option count and menu_blink ($03C6) the blink frame counter.

The arrow is the glyph tile $2B, two tiles tall like every glyph: the lower half at X in the BG3 buffer ($7F7000) and the upper half one row above (X - $40, the buffer base $7F6FC0 + X). Only the tile byte is written, the attribute stays. Blank is tile $20.

Flow: (1) DrawChoiceCursor writes the arrow and sets vram_upload_flags bit 0. (2) WaitChoiceKeysUp calls WaitFrameReadButtons and BlinkChoiceCursor until a frame reports no new button press, so the press that opened the question cannot answer it. (3) PollChoiceKeys reads one frame at a time (joy_pressed+1: $08 Up, $04 Down, $40 Y, $80 B); any other frame runs BlinkChoiceCursor and polls again. Up on the first option and Down on the last go back to step 2 (the move is ignored). A move erases the arrow (tile $20 in both halves), plays BRK #$07, resets menu_blink, moves the cell by $80 and redraws.

Exit: B plays BRK #$18 and returns carry clear, Y plays BRK #$07 and returns carry set. In both cases the arrow stays drawn (tile $2B) on the current option, A = the index pulled off the stack and X = its arrow cell. The callers then erase the window (EraseWindowFrame at text_last_window_origin, $03F7), set vram_upload_flags = 1 and either store the index in choice_result ($03D0) or, on cancel, take the cancel pointer.
=== NOTES ===
- B = confirm and Y = cancel match the walkthrough ('Press the B Button twice to equip ... Press the Y Button to exit the menu', 01-in-the-beginning.md). The other buttons are ignored here.

- ChooseMenuRow and ChooseMenuRowAtTable (lib_0118FC_part2) are the same loop for the equipment, file-select and erase menus with their own row spacing and page swap; they share BlinkChoiceCursor with this routine.
- Nothing limits the option count except the window: the largest in use is 3.

partNotes.RunChoiceMenu:
Runs one choice menu: moves the arrow between the options until B confirms or Y cancels.

When: Cop1A_ChoiceMenu (27 scripts) and Cop02_PromptYesNo, right after PrintTextString has drawn the option window.
Sees: an arrow (the ► glyph, tile $2B) in front of an option that blinks and steps with Up and Down; it stays on the answer when the menu closes.
Why: every question window of the game uses the same keys and the same arrow, so one routine serves all of them.
In: long call (JSL); M = 8; A = number of options, high byte of A = start index; X = BG3 byte offset of the first option's arrow cell (the trailing [CUR] of the option string).
Out: carry clear = B (BRK #$18), carry set = Y (BRK #$07); A = chosen index; X = the arrow cell of that option; the arrow stays drawn.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; menu_count, menu_blink, vram_upload_flags bit 0; P is not preserved (the stack is balanced).

blockNote: Blink step of the arrow cursor, shared by the choice menu and the menu-row choosers (file offsets 74507-74537, SNES $02:A30B-$A329, bank 02).
=== MODEL ===

One call per frame while a chooser waits for a key. menu_blink ($03C6) counts the calls: the low 5 bits below $18 draw the arrow (tile $2B, 24 frames), $18-$1F draw a blank (tile $20, 8 frames), so the period is 32 frames. The chooser resets the counter to 0 on every move so that the arrow is visible right after a step. Callers: RunChoiceMenu (2 sites) and the four wait loops of ChooseMenuRow and ChooseMenuRowAtTable in lib_0118FC_part2.

partNotes.BlinkChoiceCursor:
Draws the arrow or a blank in the cursor cell and advances the blink counter.

When: once per frame from the wait loops of RunChoiceMenu (2 sites) and ChooseMenuRow / ChooseMenuRowAtTable (4 sites).
Sees: the arrow blinks: on for 24 frames, off for 8.
Why: tells the player which option is selected and that the menu waits for a key.
In: near call (JSR); M = 8; X = BG3 byte offset of the arrow cell.
Out: the tile byte ($2B or $20) written to the lower half (buffer + X) and the upper half ($7F6FC0 + X); menu_blink + 1; vram_upload_flags bit 0 set. X is preserved.
Clobbers: A.

74510.text: the low 5 bits of the counter give a 32-frame blink period

The five strings of the chest and lair messages share one tail: ChestGemsFoundText holds the Gems line and, from its [::] marker (the '+M' entry), the key wait ([12]) and the erase of the dialogue box ([08:408]). The other four (LairNpcNotRecalledText, LairNpcReleasedText, ChestItemReceivedText, ChestEmptyText) end with [JMP:&ChestGemsFoundText+M]. text_arg ($03C8) is the one parameter: the NPC name index (lair record +9) for the two lair strings (through NpcNameStrings), the item id (through ItemNameList) for ChestItemReceivedText and the Gem amount as packed BCD ([06:3,03C8]) for ChestGemsFoundText; TryOpenChest picks the string by the content byte of the chest row (0 empty, $FF Gems, else an item id).
